transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-11 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Aurelius - Procurement), David Ortiz (Aurelius - Legal), Samir Rao (Aurelius - Security), Lena Gomez (Aurelius - Platform), Tom Fletcher (Aurelius - CTO, dialed in 10 min late)

Summary:
Short walkthrough of procurement gating requirements, entitlements/SSO mapping, SLA language expectations, and next steps for the security & legal review. SE to run a short benchmark and provide test account. Agreement to circulate DPA redline and SOC 2 summary.

Topics covered:
- Procurement gating checklist and approval path
- DPA / MSA redline items and exceptions
- SLA targets (p99 latency, uptime SLOs, incident response)
- KMS / encryption & key management (bring-your-own-key options)
- VPC / private deployment options and audit logging retention
- Pricing path for pilot vs production and reserved capacity

Transcript body:
00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everybody thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. Quick roll call?
00:06 Maya Patel: Maya here — procurement. We'll be taking notes for the gating checklist.
00:09 David Ortiz: David, legal.
00:10 Samir Rao: Samir on security.
00:12 Priya Nair: Priya, solutions engineering. Glad to walk through entitlements and the KMS stuff.
00:16 Lena Gomez: Hi Lena, platform.
00:18 Alex Chen: Awesome. Tom, you joined a bit late?
00:20 Tom Fletcher: Sorry, yep Tom here. On a tight timeline — we want pilot in July but procurement and legal need to clear things.
00:27 Alex Chen: Totally. Today we'll try to align on the gating items you need and spell out the steps so procurement and legal can move quickly. We'll also talk about SLA expectations and BYOK.
00:36 Maya Patel: The big questions for us: DPA/MA — do you generally accept our redlines? We also have an internal vendor gating checklist — SOC 2, data residency, SSO, RBAC, and a business continuity question.
00:49 Alex Chen: Understood. For SOC 2, Redwood is compliant and we can send the latest attestation. For DPA we usually start with our standard template but we're open to negotiating a handful of clauses. Priya, want to jump in on the entitlements?
00:59 Priya Nair: Sure, yeah. For hosted customers we have a few options: SSO via SAML/SSO/OIDC, role-based permissions, and then entitlements around who can call the API vs who can manage models/rollouts. We can map SSO groups to Redwood roles — Admin, Dev, Billing, Audit.
01:18 Lena Gomez: Do you support SCIM for automated provisioning?
01:21 Priya Nair: We do support SCIM but it's optional; currently in the hosted control plane we have SCIM provisioning for group sync. There was a small note in our docs about provisioning latency — occasionally group updates two to five minutes.
01:36 Samir Rao: For us the critical piece is KMS. We cannot have long-lived private keys stored by a third party. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
01:44 Alex Chen: Yes, we support BYOK via KMS integrations — both cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM options for private deployments. Priya, can you describe how keys are used and what logs we surface?
01:56 Priya Nair: Keys are only used to encrypt the model artifacts at rest and to wrap tenant-specific secrets. For hosted we can configure a customer KMS where Redwood has a rotating data encryption key that's itself wrapped by the customer KMS. Audit logs for key usage are surfaced in the console and can be exported to your SIEM. Note — there is an extra operational step for key rotation windows; we document recommended rotation frequency.
02:25 David Ortiz: On the DPA, we have clauses around sub-processing, data deletion timelines and data subject request support. Are deletion requests honored and auditable?
02:34 Alex Chen: Yes, we have data deletion workflows and audit logs. For hosted accounts we can present deletion proofs — time stamps and audit entries. We'll provide the DPA language and a sample deletion audit.
02:44 Maya Patel: Great. From procurement perspective we need to understand the approval path. If we agree to a pilot in July what triggers procurement to approve payment? Are you offering a trial credit?
02:55 Alex Chen: We typically offer pilot credits and short-term pilot pricing. For production, there's a reserved capacity contract — Redwood Dedicated — with monthly commits. We can share pricing tiers; Priya can run an estimate exercise if you share expected QPS and concurrency.
03:10 Priya Nair: If you can share an estimate of tokens per month and expected concurrency, we can model both hosted and dedicated costs and show the breakeven point. We also include recommendations for batching and caching.
03:25 Lena Gomez: We'll share an internal spreadsheet.
03:27 Tom Fletcher: On SLA — we need p99 latency and uptime guarantees in contract. What's typical?
03:33 Alex Chen: Our SLA for Dedicated contracts includes a p99 latency target and 99.95% uptime, with credits for SLA breaches. For hosted customers the SLA can be different; we can provide the exact language. There are also escalation windows and incident response commitments.
03:48 Samir Rao: Incident response sounds good. Does Redwood offer runbooks and post-incident RCA?
03:53 Priya Nair: Yes, for Dedicated and Private deployments we provide runbooks and we can commit to post incident RCA timelines in the MSA appendix.
04:03 David Ortiz: A couple legal asks: 1) indemnity limits; 2) data residency / subprocessor list; 3) audit rights.
04:11 Alex Chen: We'll share our subprocessors list and we can discuss audit clauses — we typically provide SOC 2 reports and limited audit rights via third party audit. On indemnity we can discuss banded caps aligned to subscription spend.
04:23 David Ortiz: OK. Also need to lock down retention for logs and how long access logs are kept.
04:28 Priya Nair: Default is 90 days for detailed logs in hosted, with longer retention options as an add-on. For Dedicated you can configure log retention in the console or push logs to your S3/SIEM.
04:40 Maya Patel: Procurement gating requires a paragraph by paragraph review. We'll flag exceptions and send them back. Can Redwood accept redlines to the DPA and MSA?
04:50 Alex Chen: Yes, we accept redlines. We prefer a prioritized list so we can negotiate the top 5 items first. We'll aim to return a counter-redline within a week of receiving them.
05:00 Tom Fletcher: Quick technical: for private deployments — if we want air-gapped — what is the installation footprint?
05:06 Priya Nair: The on-prem package includes the control plane agent and inference runtime. The runtime runs on your GPU hosts and we require outbound for licensing checks by default but can support completely air-gapped installs under an enterprise plan with a different licensing flow.
05:21 Samir Rao: Is there a remote attestation or tamper-proofing for the runtime?
05:26 Priya Nair: For air-gapped customers we have signed artifacts and support for remote attestation via HSM attestation flows, but that is an enterprise feature.
05:36 Lena Gomez: About audit logs — can we get per-token tracing? We need to tie a customer API call to an internal user id for compliance.
05:44 Priya Nair: We have request-level trace ids and can map SSO user to request tokens in the audit logs. For PII redaction we also have masking options at the ingestion layer.
05:58 Samir Rao: For KMS rotation — if you rotate the wrapping key, do we ever lose access to historical logs?
06:03 Priya Nair: No, logs are encrypted with a key rotation scheme that preserves access — wrapped keys are stored so decryption remains possible unless the customer revokes key access intentionally. We'll provide a writeup.
06:15 Alex Chen: Alright, shifting to procurement gating steps — Maya, can you outline the items you need to pass procurement?
06:21 Maya Patel: Sure. SOC 2 attestation, DPA redlines, subprocessor list, vendor questionnaire filled out, price approval from finance, and SSO/SCIM proof of concept. We also need three customer references but that can be warmed up.
06:36 Alex Chen: We can send the SOC 2 and subprocessors today, and references — we have a few prior customers who agreed to be references.
06:42 Maya Patel: Good. On pricing approvals, finance wants to see the pilot pricing and a forecast for production.
06:48 Priya Nair: We'll run a model and include a sensitivity analysis for token volume.
06:52 Tom Fletcher: Any blockers for July pilot?
06:54 Maya Patel: If legal and security can sign off on DPA and KMS, procurement can push the PO. So those are the blockers.
07:05 David Ortiz: We'll circulate DPA redlines within three business days.
07:09 Alex Chen: Great. Priya — benchmark plan?
07:12 Priya Nair: I'll provision a sandbox project and run cold-start/cached latency tests, and throughput at X tokens per second. I'll share the spreadsheet with 95/99/99.9 percentiles.
07:23 Samir Rao: We want to drive a test that simulates 2k QPS with 4k token sequences to validate memory usage.
07:31 Priya Nair: Good — we'll estimate resource needs and show Dedicated sizing.
07:35 Maya Patel: A practical procurement question — for the pilot, do you require a minimum term?
07:39 Alex Chen: Pilot credits usually have no long-term lock. Production reserved capacity has term commitments (monthly/annual). We can make the pilot zero-commit, just usage-based with credits to offset first month.
07:51 David Ortiz: On audit rights — we may want a right to audit subprocessors if high risk processes are subcontracted. Is that negotiable?
07:58 Alex Chen: We can discuss scoped audit language. Typically we provide SOC 2 and allow third-party attestation; direct audits are rare but possible with an enterprise agreement.
08:09 Tom Fletcher: Any mention of model provenance or hallucination attribution that legal would care about?
08:14 Priya Nair: From a platform POV we capture model versions and can freeze the model for a rollout so you can tie outputs back to an exact model build. For hallucination mitigation we recommend prompt tests and evals — Redwood Optimize can help with regression alerts.
08:30 Maya Patel: OK that's helpful.
08:34 Alex Chen: Wrapping up — to recap next steps: Alex to send DPA redline and SOC 2 today, Priya to send benchmark plan and provision a test account, Aurelius to send DPA redlines and entitlements mapping, and security to send KMS requirements. We'll schedule a follow-up the week after you receive our redline.
08:54 David Ortiz: Sounds good.
08:56 Maya Patel: I'll send the procurement checklist and timeline.
08:58 Tom Fletcher: Thanks all, we'll aim to review within the week.
09:02 Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. Meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker names mostly correct, some technical acronyms transcribed as spaced letters (V P C, K M S) and occasional word swaps ("key V cache" instead of KV cache). Natural speech patterns preserved.

References mentioned: link: /redwood/dpa-template (to be sent), link: /redwood/soc2-report (to be shared), spreadsheet: Benchmark-plan-template.xlsx (to be shared by SE)

End of transcript.
